✅ Answer: C. 5 years.
Under USERRA, cumulative service with one employer can total up to 5 years and the employee keeps reemployment rights. Some service doesn't count toward the 5 years, like required annual training and certain involuntary call-ups. 🇺🇸 Thank you to every veteran today.

alts:

Answer: C. 5 years. Service with one employer can total up to 5 years. Some service, like annual training and certain call-ups, doesn't count toward the cap.

👇 Comment A, B, C or D, then check the first comment for the answer.
first_comment:
✅ Answer: D. 26 weeks.
Most FMLA leave caps at 12 workweeks, but military caregiver leave allows up to 26 workweeks in a single 12-month period to care for a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness. The 26 is a combined cap, so any other FMLA leave taken in that period counts toward it.
📚 More practice: https://shrm.thegreygym.com

alts:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Under the FMLA, military caregiver leave allows an eligible employee up to how many workweeks of leave in a single 12-month period?
A. 12 weeks
B. 16 weeks
C. 20 weeks
D. 26 weeks
Answer: D. 26 weeks. Eligible employees caring for a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness can take up to 26 workweeks in a single 12-month period.

first_comment:
✅ Answer: C. 21 days.
For a valid ADEA waiver in an individual termination, the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act requires at least 21 days to consider the release. In a group layoff or exit incentive program it's 45 days. Either way, the employee then has 7 days to revoke after signing.
📚 More practice: https://shrm.thegreygym.com

alts:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Under the OWBPA, an employee age 40 or older is offered severance in exchange for a release in an individual termination. How long must they be given to consider it?
A. 7 days
B. 14 days
C. 21 days
D. 45 days
Answer: C. 21 days. In a one-person exit, the employee gets at least 21 days to consider the release (45 in a group layoff), plus 7 days to revoke after signing.
